_comment: 8 ranks with thresholds (wealth, population, buildings) and unlocked powers. Filled in during Phase 2. D2 (Phase 14): each rank's requirements is now an ARRAY of alternative requirement-groups — a ruler qualifies by satisfying ANY ONE group in full. Group 0 is always the original Prestige (palace/cathedral) path, unchanged in shape from before D2. Duke-Count add a Land/Population alt path (no palace, no downstream-gated resources — usable from turn one). Count unlocks trading houses; Margrave-Kaiser add Commerce alt paths (wealth + tradingHousesMin). Commerce unlock moved Count←Margrave and senior commerce population floors lowered in the D2 calibration pass so wealth-heavy low-pop archetypes can actually use the path — see docs/d2-rank-gate-design.md and BACKLOG.md D2.

ranks.name: Baron
ranks.description: The lowest rung of the noble ladder — but a rung, which is more than most will ever hold.

ranks.name: Duke
ranks.description: A lord of substance. Men of lower rank look up; equals keep a careful eye.

ranks.name: Prince
ranks.description: A prince commands real deference. The road to Kaiser has narrowed to a few serious contenders.

ranks.name: Count
ranks.description: A count holds enough territory and trading power to be taken seriously at the Imperial Diet.

ranks.name: Margrave
ranks.description: A margrave holds a march — border territory, real authority, and enough power to make enemies at court.

ranks.name: Archbishop
ranks.description: An archbishop walks between earthly power and divine authority. Both carry weight in the Empire.

ranks.name: King
ranks.description: A king is one step from the throne. Every rival in the Empire knows it. So does the Kaiser.

ranks.name: Kaiser
ranks.description: Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire — Victory!

_guildCharterSlotsNote: Phase 21.6. Cumulative total slots available AT that rank (not a per-promotion delta) — PLAN.md's guild design fixes Baron 1 / Duke 2 / Prince 4 / Count 5 explicitly; Margrave through Kaiser hold flat at 5 because the plan does not specify further escalation and those ranks are rarely reached inside a 60-year game (see _populationNote) — flat-and-documented beats an invented curve nobody has reviewed. One mechanism answers both 'what does promotion grant' (#49) and the design doc's open question #4 (max guild count): the cap IS the slot count.
_populationNote: Calibrated against what the simulation actually sustains. Phase 8 raised per-peasant consumption from 0.5 to 9.0, which made food a genuine constraint and LOWERED the sustainable population: realms now grow toward the land they can work (~2,400-2,600 peasants on the land an AI typically buys) and are knocked back hard by drought sequences. Earlier figures ran to 20,000 (Phase 0, before the population model existed) and then 4,200 (Phase 6, before food mattered); both made the senior ranks unreachable.
